newsitem.title: USA: Republican gets wide powers to probe Democrats.
newsitem.headline: Republican gets wide powers to probe Democrats.

text.p: After a bad tempered, meeting, Republicans on the House committee investigating campaign fund raising scandals voted their chairman wide unilateral powers to summon witnesses for legal depositions.

Dan Burton, chairman of the House Government Reform and Oversight Committee, won the ability to subpoena witnesses, order legal depositions by committee staff without the presence of members and apply for the assistance of foreign courts to conduct interviews with witnesses overseas.
The committee approved the request, voting along strict party lines over the angry opposition of Democrats who argued that Burton was voting himself unprecedented powers.
The changes to committee rules would now go to the Rules Committee and the full House of Representatives, but their approval was seen as a formality.

The committee was probing whether Asian business interests or the Chinese government tried to influence the 1996 presidential election by illegally donating funds to the Democratic Party through Asian-American intermediaries.
It was also investigating whether foreigners attempted to win influence or favours or gained access to classified information in return for their illegal financial support.
In his opening statement, Burton said the committee was possibly investigating the "largest systematic and coordinated effort to funnel illegal funds into our national elections."
"The committee has received thousands of pages of documents and has begun to piece together the intricate web of potential fund raising illegalities," he said.
Burton later said that if allegations that China tried to influence U.S. elections were proved, he would regard that as a hostile act "analagous to a military attack."

California Representative Henry Waxman, the ranking committee Democrat, called Burton's appropriation of new authority "an outrageous and partisan grab for power" and said Burton had already lost all credibility by conducting a blatantly one-sided investigation.

As tempers frayed, Florida Republican John Mica accused Democrats of "obstruction of justice" while Wisconsin Democrat Robert Wise threatened to block future Republican requests to grant witnesses immunity in exchange for their testimony, for which a two thirds committee vote would be needed.
Georgia Republican Bob Barr called that a "raw, brutal threat...I don't think the American people will stand for that."

Summing up, Waxman asked: "Why should we have to trust you, Mr Chairman? We have seen no evidence of any fairness whatsoever. Well, vote us down! And then tell the American people you've got a fair bipartisan investigation, because none of us believe it!"
Many key witnesses have either taken refuge in Asian countries or invoked their right under the Fifth Amendment to the U.S. Constitution to refuse to answer questions.
Burton said investigators needed to interview between 150 and 200 witnesses. The size of the task made it necessary for him to request the new powers.
Democrats said Burton had already unilaterally issued over 150 subpoenas for documents and had received 320,000 pages from Democrat sources and only 15 documents from Republican sources.
